finding.claim: deleteAccount has no authorization check. The result of canDelete() is discarded, so any authenticated user can delete any account by id.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled path parameter id (DELETE /accounts/{id}) plus any authenticated User u. Precondition: caller is a non-admin who knows or guesses an id they do not own.

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) accepts caller and target id
Account a = accounts.get(id) loads the target
canDelete(u, a) called but boolean return ignored; nothing enforced

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (lines 9-11) is logically correct but never enforced on this path; assertCanDelete (lines 13-17) is not called here; no other check in lines 20-24; caller authentication is outside this directory and unverified.

verdict.guard_found: None on the deleteAccount path. canDelete (src/AccountService.java:9-11) returns a bool that is discarded as a bare statement at line 22. assertCanDelete (lines 13-17) is not called in deleteAccount; it is only used by closeAccount at line 29. No other check exists in the directory (grep found no @PreAuthorize or other guard on DELETE /accounts/{id}).
verdict.reason: deleteAccount at src/AccountService.java:20-23 calls canDelete(u, a) at line 22 without testing its result, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any caller and any existing account id, while closeAccount at line 29 shows the intended pattern (assertCanDelete throws). The caller-authentication and HTTP route wiring live outside this directory and were not verified, so the reachable-by-any-user part relies on the claim's stated precondition.

finding.claim: Unknown account ids cause a NullPointerException for non-admin callers, creating an existence oracle once F1 is fixed.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled id in deleteAccount (line 20) and closeAccount (line 27). Precondition: non-admin authenticated caller.
finding.sink: a.ownerId() at src/AccountService.java:10 dereferences null when accounts.get(id) returns null.

trace.note: accounts.get(id) returns null for nonexistent id (same at line 28 for closeAccount)
canDelete called with a = null (same at line 29 via assertCanDelete)
a.ownerId() throws NullPointerException for non-admins; admin short-circuits at u.admin() and avoids the dereference

finding.guards_checked: No null check on accounts.get(id) in either method; admin path short-circuits so admins get silent success on missing ids.

verdict.guard_found: none. No null check on accounts.get(id) at src/AccountService.java:21 or :28. The canDelete result at line 22 is a bare statement, so its return value is discarded. assertCanDelete (line 13-17) calls canDelete, which dereferences a.ownerId() at line 10 before any throw can happen. Nothing catches the NPE in this file. The admin short-circuit at line 10 (u.admin() evaluated first) is the only path that avoids the dereference.
verdict.reason: For a non-admin caller, canDelete at src/AccountService.java:10 evaluates a.ownerId() on a null Account returned by accounts.get(id) at lines 21 and 28, so an unknown id throws NullPointerException, while admins take the u.admin() short-circuit. The trace is accurate, but the "existence oracle" framing depends on how the unseen HTTP layer maps that exception to a response, which this file does not show.
